tier_reason: Every Robyn and competitor rps figure matches site/data/results/robyn.json and the sibling nginx, h2o, agensio, drogon, cutelyst and libreactorng JSON files in MDA2AV/HttpArena; the code is public (frameworks/robyn/{Dockerfile,app.py,requirements.txt}, frameworks/nginx/{Dockerfile,nginx.conf,ngx_http_httparena_module.c}, scripts/lib/profiles.sh), nginx flags and the CPU (site/data/current.json) are stated. Not A because Robyn runs as the prebuilt PyPI wheel robyn==0.83.0, whose rustc version and target flags are not published (TrueAsync precedent), although its Cargo release profile (opt-level 3, fat LTO, codegen-units 1) is public.

corrections.baseline: nginx 1.31.4 (C) with the custom ngx_http_httparena_module, ./configure --with-cc-opt='-O3 -march=native -DNDEBUG' on debian:trixie build-essential, worker_processes auto; its /pipeline handler returns a constant 'ok'. The Dockerfile links the distribution libssl-dev rather than building quictls (the quictls mentions in its comment, README and meta.json are stale), which does not matter for the HTTP/1.1 rows. Other rows in the same suite: h2o, mongoose, libreactorng, libioma (C) and Drogon, userver, proxygen, agensio, cutelyst (C++).
corrections.claimed_speedup: pipelined-4096 (16x pipelining, marked reference-only and excluded from the composite score in the HttpArena README): 16,183,222 req/s vs nginx 4,037,345 (4.01x), h2o 4,938,603 (3.28x), agensio 4,958,241 (3.26x), Drogon 7,801,404 (2.07x), cutelyst 10,167,331 (1.59x); libreactorng 43,424,448 is far ahead (0.37x), and actix-web, the Rust server Robyn runs on, scores 16,338,425 on the same row (Robyn 0.99x). Far behind on the scored rows: baseline-4096 430,749 vs nginx 3,284,513 (0.13x), limited-conn-4096 320,875 vs 2,626,297 (0.12x), latency-1m-1024 416,289 vs libreactorng 998,522 (0.42x). Extra row not in the original record: async-32000 (10 ms delay, 32,000 connections) 309,871 vs Drogon 143,001 (2.17x) and cutelyst 761,563 (0.41x). All ratios derived from page data.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Robyn: python:3.13-slim image, pip install robyn==0.83.0 (prebuilt wheel; Cargo.toml at v0.83.0 sets [profile.release] opt-level = 3, lto = 'fat', codegen-units = 1, panic = 'abort', but the rustc version and target-cpu of the published wheel are not stated); app.py runs processes = min(sched_getaffinity, 128) and workers = 2, and /pipeline is declared @app.get('/pipeline', const=True). C side: nginx 1.31.4 -O3 -march=native -DNDEBUG (debian:trixie gcc from build-essential).
corrections.hardware: HttpArena machine per site/data/current.json: AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO 3995WX 64-Cores (64 cores, 128 threads), 251 GiB RAM, Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, kernel 6.17.0-22-generic, Docker 29.3.0 (runc), governor performance. Per scripts/lib/profiles.sh the server container is pinned to cpuset 0-31,64-95 (32 cores, 64 threads) for the baseline, pipelined, limited-conn, async and latency-1m profiles (0-3,64-67 for latency-500k-8cpu); load from gcannon (-p 16 for pipelined). current.json is undated.
corrections.workload: HttpArena HTTP/1.1 profiles for the Robyn entry (Robyn 0.83.0 on Python 3.13, uvloop engine): pipelined-4096 is GET /pipeline with 16 requests pipelined per batch over 4096 connections; on Robyn this is a const=True route whose 'ok' response is cached in the Rust layer, so no Python code runs per request and the row measures Robyn's Rust core on actix-web 4. baseline-4096 (GET/POST /baseline11 with query parsing in a Python handler), limited-conn-4096 (10 requests per connection) and latency-1m-1024 (offered rate pinned at 1M req/s) do run Python handlers.
corrections.caveats: The only win is the pipelined row, and it is not a Python result: /pipeline is a const route cached in Robyn's Rust layer on actix-web 4, and Robyn's 16,183,222 req/s matches actix-web's own HttpArena row (16,338,425), so the win belongs to actix-web (already listed in wave 14 at tier A); this record is a candidate duplicate of https://github.com/actix/actix-web. The HttpArena README marks pipelined as reference-only and excludes it from the composite score; every fast pipelined handler beats the nginx module there (nginx 4.04M vs libreactorng 43.4M), so the 4x says more about nginx's pipelined path than about Robyn. On every scored row that runs Python Robyn is 2.4x to 8x slower than nginx or libreactorng. Cross-run comparison: Robyn's baseline, pipelined, limited-conn and upload rows are unchanged since the per-framework results split (commit 5698fa8, 2026-07-24), while the nginx rows come from commit df1a679 (2026-08-20; the earlier 0a18672 nginx rows differ by 2% or less on these rows); upload-256 and upload-32 rows are stale (that profile was replaced by echo-100k on 2026-08-30). Results files are undated single 5 s runs with no repeat count. The extra async-32000 win over Drogon is weak evidence: Drogon's /delay handler schedules every reply on app().getLoop(), the main event loop rather than the connection's I/O loop, which likely bottlenecks it on one thread (not verified by profiling). Robyn's README cites TechEmpower Round 22 plaintext in an image and compares only with Python frameworks, not C servers. Robyn's Rust build flags come from the published wheel and are not stated beyond the Cargo release profile.
corrections.why_faster: On the pipelined row the Python handler never runs: Robyn serves the const=True /pipeline route from a response cached in its Rust layer, so the row measures actix-web 4's HTTP/1.1 pipelining (Robyn 16,183,222 vs actix-web 16,338,425 req/s) against the nginx module's pipelined path; both sides return a constant 'ok', so the work is equivalent. Why nginx trails on pipelining is not stated in the sources. On rows that run Python, Robyn is 2.4x to 8x slower.

notes: Numbers verified against the HttpArena results JSONs, tier B kept (prebuilt wheel, TrueAsync precedent), verdict downgrade because the claim is not a Python or Robyn result: the pipelined win is a const route cached in Rust on actix-web 4 and equals actix-web's own row, so consider recording it as a duplicate of https://github.com/actix/actix-web. Shortcomings to record: only win is the reference-only pipelined row (excluded from the composite score), 0.12x to 0.42x of nginx or libreactorng on scored rows, cross-run rows (Robyn rows from 2026-07-24 or earlier against nginx rows from 2026-08-20), unstated wheel build flags. Metadata confirmed: BSD-2-Clause, 7.4k stars, last commit 2026-08-09, not a fork, not archived.

tier_reason: No opened page supports a Caddy win over a configured nginx: the 4x exists only as an HN submission title (the linked post, manishrjain.com/reverse-proxy-caddy-nginx, did not resolve), the benchmark_url's one Caddy win (256K mean latency 1.310211 ms vs 1.536594 ms) came from an untuned nginx.conf and reversed to nginx 1.23x faster after the author's tuning commit 7cb9315c (crippled-baseline precedent), and HttpArena (public code, A-grade suite) shows Caddy 0.07x to 0.25x of nginx on every shared row.

corrections.claimed_speedup: No verified win. 'Caddy Outperforms Nginx 4x' is the title of HN item 33725154 (snippet only; the post at https://manishrjain.com/reverse-proxy-caddy-nginx, which the benchmark README credits as its inspiration, could not be opened: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND). patrickdappollonio/nginx-vs-caddy-benchmark (Vegeta, fixed rate 500 req/s for 10 s, HTTPS reverse proxy to a local container): hello-docker response mean latency nginx 337.36 us vs Caddy 385.502 us (nginx 14% faster per the README); 256K file first run Caddy 1.310211 ms vs nginx 1.536594 ms (Caddy 1.17x, derived from page data) with an untuned nginx.conf; after commit 7cb9315c tuned nginx, nginx 1.192198 ms vs Caddy 1.471049 ms (nginx 23% faster per the README). HttpArena (Caddy v2.8.4 serving directly, not proxying): baseline-4096 431,894 vs nginx 3,284,513 req/s (0.13x), limited-conn-4096 237,689 vs 2,626,297 (0.09x), pipelined-4096 761,137 vs 4,037,345 (0.19x), json-tls-4096 321,964 vs 1,313,755 (0.25x), static-tls-1024 159,177 vs 720,869 (0.22x), baseline-h3-64 360,511 vs 4,849,624 (0.07x); ratios derived from page data.
corrections.workload: Claim: HTTPS reverse proxying (HN title only). Opened benchmark: Vegeta open-loop attack at 500 req/s for 10 s against https://localhost/ through Caddy or nginx in Docker, proxying to patrickdappollonio/hello-docker (20-byte reply) or to docker-http-server serving a 256K data.bin; metric is latency at a fixed rate, not throughput. Cross-check: HttpArena HTTP/1.1, TLS, h2 and h3 origin-serving profiles with custom Go handler modules in Caddy and a custom C module in nginx.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: patrickdappollonio benchmark: unpinned caddy:latest and nginx:latest images, no versions or build flags stated. HttpArena cross-check: Caddy v2.8.4 built with xcaddy on golang:1.22-bookworm with the httparena and httparena_json handler modules; nginx 1.31.4 built with --with-cc-opt='-O3 -march=native -DNDEBUG'.
corrections.hardware: patrickdappollonio benchmark: laptop, 6-core Intel Core i7-10710U, 15.7 GB RAM, Pop!_OS 22.04 LTS, kernel 6.0.6. HttpArena: AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO 3995WX (64 cores, 128 threads), server container pinned to cpuset 0-31,64-95 (32 cores, 64 threads) per scripts/lib/profiles.sh.
corrections.caveats: Recorded as an unsupported and contradicted claim. The 4x figure is only an HN submission title; the post could not be opened, so its method, versions and configs are unknown. In the opened benchmark (11 stars, no license, 'quick-and-dirty' by its own description) the first nginx.conf had worker_connections 1024 and no sendfile, access_log or upstream HTTP/1.1 settings, so nginx logged every request and proxied over HTTP/1.0 while Caddy ran with its defaults; the author's commit 7cb9315c tuned nginx (worker_connections 4000, access_log off, sendfile, proxy_http_version 1.1) and nginx then won the 256K test by 23% on mean, 13% on p95 and 11% on p99; nginx had already won the hello test by 14% before tuning. The tuned config still has no upstream keepalive directive. Images are unpinned :latest, single runs at a fixed 500 req/s. HttpArena shows Caddy 4x to 14x slower than nginx on every shared row, but it tests Caddy v2.8.4 (2024, Go 1.22) as an origin server with custom handler modules rather than as a reverse proxy, and the Caddy rows (commit 0a18672, 2026-08-15) and nginx rows (commit df1a679, 2026-08-20) come from different runs; the nginx rows at 0a18672 are within about 2% of the later ones on baseline, limited-conn and pipelined and 9% higher on json-tls, so the gap holds either way. The Caddy README makes no performance claim against nginx.
corrections.why_faster: Not faster on any opened evidence. The one Caddy win in the patrickdappollonio benchmark came from nginx's untuned config (per-request access logging, HTTP/1.0 upstream, default worker settings) against Caddy's defaults and disappeared once nginx was tuned.

notes: Downgraded C to D: no opened page shows Caddy beating a configured nginx; the 4x is an HN title only, the benchmark_url's 1.17x win came from an untuned nginx.conf and reversed to nginx 23% faster after the author's tuning commit 7cb9315c, and HttpArena shows Caddy at 0.07x to 0.25x of nginx (origin serving, Caddy v2.8.4, cross-run rows). Shortcomings to record: not faster, claim unverifiable (post unreachable), crippled nginx config in the only win, unpinned images, latency at a fixed 500 req/s rather than throughput. Metadata confirmed: Apache-2.0, 77.8k stars, last commit 2026-10-10, not a fork, not archived.

tier_reason: No numbers anywhere reachable: the README on the default branch develop-3.x says only 'Predictable performance - fast and consistent under load, right out of the box', the develop-2.x and main READMEs only say 'High performance', the repo has no benchmark directory or docs page on performance, HttpArena has no Ferron entry (site/data/results/ferron.json 404), and the project website (ferron.sh) did not resolve.

corrections.caveats: The README (default branch develop-3.x) says only 'Predictable performance - fast and consistent under load, right out of the box. No runtime tuning required.'; older branches say 'High performance - thoroughly optimized for speed' (develop-2.x) and 'built with Rust's async capabilities for optimal speed' (main, develop). No benchmark code, data or methodology is in the repository (docs/ holds configuration, installation, migration, module-development and use-cases pages only), and Ferron has no HttpArena entry. The website charts could not be opened (ferron.sh: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND), so nothing was measured or read; the HN statements in the record (nginx left out of the static-file charts, Ferron roughly on par with nginx as a reverse proxy) are snippet only. Kept as a tier D claim with no numbers for notability (2.2k stars) and for a verifier with wider network access to read the website charts. A web search for Ferron benchmarks returned nothing about Ferron itself.

notes: Tier D confirmed: no numbers in the repo, no HttpArena entry, website unreachable; claim is marketing only and HN snippets say it is on par with nginx, not faster. Shortcomings to record: no benchmark data or methodology, website charts reportedly omit nginx from static-file tests (snippet only).
